body.statement: For \(N=4\), determine a nonempty two-dimensional parameter cell \(J\), an explicit optimizing channel family, and an attaining certificate \(\Gamma_J\) for which one algebraically isolated endpoint lies on the boundary of \(\mathcal B_{4,\alpha}\); prove the sign of \(\Delta_{4,\alpha}(\lambda)\) on both adjacent cells and identify which channel support or confidence active set changes at that endpoint.
body.justification: This node is retained as the exact unresolved structural question whose solution would be needed before advertising a balanced-binary phase boundary.
body.gap: No optimizer-attaining global certificate, nonempty equality cell, frontier polynomial, transverse root, adjacent sign pair, or active-set transition has been proved from the frozen primitives and exact artifacts.
body.consumer: Only a future resolution could yield a certified switch point between one-bit and richer hidden-assignment reporting protocols; the current results provide an exclusion interval, not such a threshold.

obligation.what_is_open: Construct a nonempty open semialgebraic region in the \(\lambda\)--\(\alpha\) plane on which one specified balanced \(m=2\) binary partition is globally optimal over every common private channel and confidence rule, and continue an attaining certificate to an algebraically isolated transverse frontier with a strict adjacent nonbinary separation.
obligation.obstruction: The available unrestricted certificate is not optimizer-attaining: at \(\lambda=1000\) and \(\alpha=2/5\) its certified lower and feasible upper values differ by \(297/50000000\), while the entire interval \([999.9,1000.1]\) is already certified to lie outside \(\mathcal B_{4,2/5}\). Fixed-binary confidence duals at \(\lambda=2,3,10,100\) leave nonzero global polarization gaps, so fixed-channel optimality does not furnish the simultaneous lower saddle required by \(\Gamma_J\). Semialgebraicity alone gives only a finite list of possible contacts and does not prove that an equality cell is nonempty or select a frontier polynomial.
obligation.attempted: Reused the exact fixed-channel primal--dual extractions, the full fourteen-weight channel representation, all \(41^4=2825761\) polarized vertex-tensor bounds at the certified point, the robust dual refinement, the balanced-binary duals at four additional privacy budgets, and the established certificate-characterization theorem. I also audited the supplied exact certificate payloads for a matching binary primal/global-dual value or a recorded continuing active set; none is present. Because every available simultaneous lower bound remains strict at its proposed binary candidate, there is no equality identity to continue and hence no honest endpoint polynomial, isolating interval, sign pair, or active-set-change event to report.
obligation.partial_result:
At \(N=4\), \(\alpha=2/5\), and \(\lambda=1000\), the exact certificates prove
\[
\frac{129113957}{50000000}
\le L^\star_{4,2/5}(1000)
\le \frac{64557127}{25000000},
\]
whose width is \(297/50000000\).  They also prove that every optimizer uses \(m=2\) at this point, that every optimizer uses \(m=2\) for \(\lambda\ge1000\) when \(\alpha=2/5\), and that
\[
[999.9,1000.1]\cap\mathcal B_{4,2/5}=\varnothing.
\]
The semialgebraic characterization reduces any future certified boundary to finitely many basis-determinant, inactive-slack, residual-contact, or candidate-value-difference polynomial contacts.  None of the checked certificates attains the unrestricted optimum at a balanced binary channel, so these results neither exhibit a nonempty equality cell nor locate one of its boundary points.
